headline: Fresh US-Iran strikes over the Strait of Hormuz push oil up roughly 4% and drag the KSE-100 down 1.27% to 179,927.04 on its worst breadth in weeks (13 up, 87 down) — the desk narrows its favour to banks, fertilizer and E&P while sitting out autos, cement, OMCs and textiles.
summary: Over the weekend the US and Iran traded fresh strikes around the Strait of Hormuz — Iran says the strait is closed, US CENTCOM disputes that — and oil jumped on the news, with Brent up 4.04% on the day to $79.08. Since well over 80% of Pakistan's crude imports transit that strait, PSX reacted fast: the KSE-100 closed at 179,927.04, down 2,314.73 points (-1.27%), with a very weak 13 stocks rising against 87 falling. The desk's macro read has moved to risk-off, and while banks, fertilizer and E&P carry the fundamental and rate-carry logic to stay favoured through this, today's tape sold off almost everything indiscriminately — the one real bright spot was refineries, up on a same-day $6bn government refinery-upgrade policy plan rather than on the oil move itself. For now the desk is leaning toward names that stack sector logic, real fundamentals and a dated catalyst together, and staying patient on everything else.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: SBP's 11.5% policy rate (next MPC decision 2026-07-27) keeps the sector's rate-carry logic intact, even though the whole group traded red today (UBL -1.58%, MCB -1.16%, HBL -0.91%, NBP -2.52%) in the broad selloff.

sectors.name: Fertilizer
sectors.why: Low direct oil-import exposure and defensive domestic demand — FFC (beta 0.28) and ENGROH (beta 0.05) barely move with the index, which is exactly the ballast the desk wants while Hormuz headlines whip the tape.

sectors.name: E&P
sectors.why: Structurally the direct beneficiary of pricier crude (OGDC net margin 40%, PPL 34%, MARI 49%), though today's price action didn't reward that logic yet — all three still closed lower (OGDC -0.76%, MARI -1.28%, PPL -1.75%) inside the same broad risk-off sweep.

sectors.name: Refineries
sectors.why: Reconciled up from macro's blanket avoid: a fresh government plan to fast-track $6bn of refinery upgrades made ATRL (+1.93%), NRL (+2.05%) and PRL (+1.57%) today's rare green names, but margins stay exposed to volatile, weekly-repriced crude costs if Hormuz worsens — a genuine two-sided call, not a clean favour.

sectors.name: OMCs
sectors.why: PSO's net margin is a wafer-thin 1.4%, and with pricing reviews now weekly given the volatility, the July 11 fuel hike (petrol +Rs13.18, diesel +Rs13.80/litre) passes straight through to consumers rather than boosting OMC profit.

sectors.name: Autos
sectors.why: A softer rupee and pricier imported parts squeeze margins right as June's passenger-car sales fell 12.9% YoY even as FY26 cumulative sales ran up 39.4%; HCAR (-1.77% today, -13.03% over 20 sessions) and GAL both carry the desk's only two live technical triggers today, but both sit in this macro-flagged sector — a real tension, not a green light.

sectors.name: Cement
sectors.why: Energy-intensive and import-cost exposed — DGKC (-3.20%), MLCF (-3.17%) and FCCL (-2.97%) were among today's worst-performing KSE-100 names.

sectors.name: Textiles / exporters
sectors.why: Gulf freight-cost and input-cost exposure amid the Hormuz disruption; NML fell -2.28% today and is down 7.86% over five sessions.

watchlist.angle: Banks are one of the desk's three favoured sectors this cycle (SBP holding at 11.5%, next MPC 2026-07-27). HBL screens 'attractive' on fundamentals — 6.95x trailing P/E in the cheapest third of PSX, a 7.65% dividend yield covered by a 48% payout, and a forward P/E of 6.46 below trailing pointing to expected earnings growth. It also held up better than most of the sector today (-0.91% vs UBL -1.58% and NBP -2.52%), stayed above both its 20- and 50-day averages (RSI 59.2), and sits in the desk's top-10 predictability list (score 59.1). Results are due 2026-08-11.
watchlist.risk: It still fell alongside the whole banking sector today — being macro-favoured doesn't make it immune to a risk-off sweep — and there's no dated catalyst before the Aug 11 results to force a re-rating in the meantime.

watchlist.angle: Also favoured-sector banking and 'attractive' on the fundamentals screen: 8.52x trailing P/E, a 6.61% yield covered at a 56% payout, and a 30.3% net margin. Unlike most of the tape it's still above both its 20- and 50-day averages (RSI 62.6) and up 19.4% over the past 20 sessions even after today's -1.58% dip, and it carries the nearest dated catalyst on the desk's board — results on 2026-07-22.
watchlist.risk: UBL was one of the names newslog specifically flagged as trading red in today's Hormuz-driven selloff — a fresh escalation before the July 22 results could easily overwhelm the earnings catalyst.

watchlist.angle: Fertilizer is the desk's other favoured sector — low direct oil-import exposure, defensive domestic demand (beta 0.28). FFC carries the single highest predictability score on the whole desk (67.3), and its most-proven setup on its own history, a 52-week-high breakout, has fired with a 77.8% hit rate historically (71.4% out-of-sample, +3.17% net expectancy per trade) — though it isn't triggering today (RSI 47.4, price 4.4% below its 20-day high). Results are due 2026-07-29, and a forward P/E of 7.02 below trailing 9.39 points to expected earnings growth.
watchlist.risk: No live trigger is firing right now, so this is a name to watch rather than an active setup — and fertilizer was last week's single worst-hit sector by index points per the Mettis weekly roundup, a reminder the 'defensive' label isn't absolute.

watchlist.angle: E&P is macro's third favoured sector — the direct structural beneficiary of the pricier crude behind today's headlines. OGDC screens 'mixed' but with real substance: a 40% net margin, a forward P/E of 7.85 below trailing 9.24, and it was the most resilient of the big three E&P names today (-0.76% vs PPL -1.75% and MARI -1.28%). Its proven 52-week-high breakout setup carries a 63% historical hit rate on its own history.
watchlist.risk: Today's price action didn't actually reward the 'oil beneficiary' logic — OGDC still closed lower with everything else — and the next earnings date isn't until 2026-09-23, so this is a structural, fundamentals-led case for now rather than a near-term catalyst trade.

watchlist.angle: The day's single most concrete news catalyst: a government plan announced today to fast-track $6bn of refinery upgrades, offering a seven-year duty-protection package to refiners that sign an OGRA Upgrade Agreement within 90 days — ATRL is one of the named beneficiaries. It was one of only five KSE-100 gainers today (+1.93%), trades above both its 20- and 50-day averages on a volume surge (1.95x average), and is cheap on paper (P/E 4.53, bottom third of PSX).
watchlist.risk: Refineries sit on macro's original avoid list for a reason — margins stay exposed to volatile, weekly-repriced crude costs if Hormuz worsens, RSI is already at 63.7 after today's pop, and the fundamental picture is 'mixed' with a thin 7.4% net margin; good policy news doesn't erase that near-term cost risk.

catalysts.event: SBP MPC — first FY27 monetary policy decision; watched for a hawkish tilt if the oil shock persists into the CPI print
PBS July 2026 CPI release — first print to capture the July 11 fuel-price hike
MEBL, LUCK, MCB, MARI, FCCL results (scraped estimates, unconfirmed)
HBL, POL, ATRL, NRL results (scraped estimates, unconfirmed)

risks: A confirmed, sustained Hormuz closure or a wider US-Iran war would extend the oil shock — Pakistan's own Ministry of Economic Affairs has warned that a prior phase of this same conflict (April 2026) tripled the weekly oil import bill from roughly $300mn to $800mn, and PIDE has flagged CPI could re-accelerate to 15-17% YoY under a severe, sustained disruption.

GCC states supply 55% of Pakistan's remittances (4.7% of GDP) — a prolonged Gulf slowdown tied to this conflict could squeeze that inflow channel just as the current account is trying to hold a surplus.

Today's breadth was about as weak as it gets (13 up, 87 down) — a reminder that even the desk's favoured names (UBL, HBL, NBP all traded red today) can get swept up in indiscriminate selling if the news flow worsens before it stabilizes.
